scope: Game-design questions and user answers only. Original options preserved when available. Dates in file names are America/Los_Angeles; provenance timestamps are UTC.
completeness: Recovered entries only; missing answers are explicitly marked. This is not a complete export of every chat or every historical interview.

entries.question:
❓ Q1 — Where should the two easy rounds apply?

➡️ I recommend easy rounds 1–2 at the start of the whole run. Later arenas open with fewer enemies and the 10% enemy-health drop, while keeping the strength earned through previous arenas.
options: Easy first two rounds of the run (recommended)
Easy first two rounds in every arena
entries.answer: Easy first two rounds of the run (recommended)
entries.interpretation: Historical answer; current rules and later corrections are in ../../current.json.

entries.question:
❓ Q2 — How should we make those opening rounds forgiving?

➡️ I recommend fewer enemies plus lower incoming damage, then ramp both up. The current prototype starts solo with six enemies total, two arriving together, and half the previous opening damage.
options: Fewer enemies; keep current enemy damage
entries.interpretation: Historical answer; current rules and later corrections are in ../../current.json.

entries.question:
❓ Q3 — After the opening, what should drive the rising pressure?

➡️ I recommend enemy numbers, overlapping arrivals and tougher role combinations leading the increase, with health and damage growing more gradually. The 10% health drop will use the previous arena’s final round as its baseline.
options: Health and damage rise just as strongly
